title: Exploring the Perplexing Ruins: Fallen, Campaign Notebook, Hilgaarb and more
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KiOKGmcOb_g

Daniel (@dungeondive) surveys the itch.io catalogue of Perplexing Ruins — designer Allan's *Fallen*, its city supplement *Hilgaarb*, and a physical campaign notebook — then demonstrates how he'd combine them into an actual solo adventure.

*Fallen* is baroque, grim fantasy set roughly 1600–1850: stagecoach roads, alchemy, witchcraft, strange lights in the bell tower, with *Brotherhood of the Wolf* as a touchstone. Daniel walks the mechanics in detail. Four stats with luck dice you can spend or hold as a bonus; a rank system (d6 down to d4) where wounds drop your rank and harm chips its pips; 2d6 tests split into clean success, complication, and miss. The parts he singles out are the usage die — every consumable tracked by a die that steps down on a 1 or 2, giving survival texture with almost no bookkeeping — and skills whose entries spell out the narrative outcome for each result band. Spellcasting works off a dice pool spent to trigger spell words: combine "bone" and "explode" and describe what happens.

He closes by building a five-stage journey through Hilgaarb using *Untold Encounters of the Random Kind* — grave-robbing a councilman's ring to clear a debt, complete with a prize bull that gores him on the way in.

----

Does the usage die strike the right balance for survival mechanics, or do you prefer tracking supplies exactly?
